---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 6.1: bootstrap estimates (pathologists)"
---

Step 6.1 of the paper simulation (pathologist design): bootstrap estimates and 95 % quantile intervals
(QI) of recall, precision and F1 for every dataset of step 2.1 (600 datasets) with four resampling
schemes. The comparison with the truths of step 2.1 follows in the evaluation (step 7 and
`S3_Code_Simulation_Coverage.Rmd`).

The estimates are included in `simulation/estimates_pathologists/06_1_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz`.

**Resampling schemes** (K = 10,000 draws each, as in the example Rmds and step 6)

| method | Resampled per draw | As in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | all rows (image × pathologist) with replacement | example, 1st chunk of the average pathologist |
| `stratified` | the images **within** each pathologist (strata = pathologists), independently per pathologist | example, 2nd chunk and single pathologist |
| `cluster` | the images (clusters), each with the rows of **all** pathologists | cluster bootstrap over images |
| `two_way` | the pathologists **and** the images, independently with replacement, all combinations | two-way (pigeonhole) bootstrap for crossed designs (Owen 2007) |

**Estimands** (same names as in step 5.1)

- `average_pathologist`: per draw pooled / grouped over all resampled rows (`row`, `cluster`,
  `two_way`; the `stratified` bootstrap is at the level of `row` and not used in the paper).
- `single_pathologist`: per draw and pathologist pooled / grouped, the draws of all pathologists
  combined into one distribution (as in the example; `stratified` and `cluster`). Not for `row` (no
  pathologist structure) and not for `two_way` (resampling the pathologists does not change the
  combined distribution of the per-pathologist values, so it equals `cluster`).

**Metrics**

- pooled: Recall = Σ TP / Σ P, Precision = Σ TP / Σ (TP + FP) (0 if there are no detections),
  F1 = 2 Σ TP / Σ (2 TP + FN + FP).
- grouped: mean of the per-cell metrics (cell = image × pathologist). F1 = 2 TP / (2 TP + FN + FP)
  is always defined (P ≥ 1), precision of a cell without detections = 0 (paper "Case B").
- `value`: median of the bootstrap draws. `value_observed`: the point estimate, i.e. the metric of
  the original dataset (average pathologist only; name as in step 6).
- Interval: 95 % QI (percentile interval).

**Seed** (offset from `01_seed_offsets.csv`)

- `seed + 2000000` per dataset (the ML bootstrap of step 6 uses the same offset on other data).
  The four methods are drawn one after another from this seed.
- The mirai daemons use the L'Ecuyer-CMRG random number generator (not R's default
  Mersenne-Twister); in a normal R session, set `RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")` first.

**Run**

- Parallel with `purrr::map()` and `in_parallel()` on mirai daemons, one dataset at a time. The
  methods are computed one after another (about 10^7 rows per method for 23 pathologists).

**Output** (`simulation/estimates_pathologists/`)

- `06_1_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz`: `scenario`, `n_slide`, `rep`, `variant`, `model`, `model_id`,
  `estimand`, `averaging`, `name`, `interval`, `value`, `value_observed`, `.lower`, `.upper`
  (same columns as `05_1_bayes_estimates.csv.xz` plus `value_observed`,
  `model_id = "bootstrap_<method>"`).

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# Median and 95% quantile interval (QI) of grouped draws (column value), one row per group
median_interval <- function(df) {
  median_qi(df, value) |>
    mutate(interval = "qi") |>
    select(-.width, -.point, -.interval)
}

# Pooled and grouped metrics per group of a (grouped) data frame of cells
calc_metrics <- function(df) {
  df |>
    summarise(
      # POOLED: sum the counts first, then compute the metrics
      Precision_pooled  = pmax(0, sum(TP) / sum(TP + FP), na.rm = TRUE), # 0 if there are no detections
      Recall_pooled     = sum(TP) / sum(TP + FN),
      F1_pooled         = 2 * sum(TP) / sum(2 * TP + FN + FP),
      # GROUPED: average the per-cell metrics (each cell same weight)
      Precision_grouped = mean(Precision),
      Recall_grouped    = mean(Recall),
      F1_grouped        = mean(F1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(matches("_(pooled|grouped)$"), names_to = c("name", "averaging"), names_sep = "_")
}

# The four resampling schemes. Each returns one row per bootstrap draw (.draw = 1..K) and
# resampled cell (image x pathologist), with the counts and per-cell metrics of df_cells.
# cross_join() with .draw = 1:K gives one independent bootstrap "study" per draw (as in the example).

# Row bootstrap (example, 1st chunk): all rows are resampled with replacement
bootstrap_row <- function(df_cells, K) {
  df_cells |>
    cross_join(tibble(.draw = seq_len(K))) |>
    group_by(.draw) |>
    slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |>
    ungroup()
}

# Stratified bootstrap (example, 2nd chunk and single pathologist): the images are resampled
# within each pathologist, independently per pathologist
bootstrap_stratified <- function(df_cells, K) {
  df_cells |>
    cross_join(tibble(.draw = seq_len(K))) |>
    group_by(.draw, rater_ID) |>
    slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |>
    ungroup()
}

# Cluster bootstrap over images: the images are resampled, each with the rows of all pathologists
bootstrap_cluster <- function(df_cells, K) {
  distinct(df_cells, slide) |>
    cross_join(tibble(.draw = seq_len(K))) |>
    group_by(.draw) |>
    slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |>
    ungroup() |>
    left_join(df_cells, by = "slide", relationship = "many-to-many")
}

# Two-way bootstrap: the images and the pathologists are resampled independently,
# the draw contains all combinations of the resampled images and pathologists
bootstrap_two_way <- function(df_cells, K) {
  df_slides <- distinct(df_cells, slide) |>
    cross_join(tibble(.draw = seq_len(K))) |>
    group_by(.draw) |>
    slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |>
    ungroup()

  df_raters <- distinct(df_cells, rater_ID) |>
    cross_join(tibble(.draw = seq_len(K))) |>
    group_by(.draw) |>
    slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |>
    ungroup()

  inner_join(df_slides, df_raters, by = ".draw", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    left_join(df_cells, by = c("slide", "rater_ID"))
}

# Bootstrap of one pathologist dataset with the four resampling schemes (one after another)
bootstrap_pathologist_metrics <- function(df_sim, K = 10000) {
  # Per-cell metrics for grouped averaging
  df_cells <- df_sim |>
    mutate(
      Precision = pmax(0, TP / (TP + FP), na.rm = TRUE), # Set to 0 if TP + FP = 0
      Recall    = TP / (TP + FN),                         # P >= 1
      F1        = 2 * TP / (2 * TP + FN + FP)
    )

  # Resampled datasets of the four methods (one row per draw and resampled cell),
  # used for both estimands
  df_draws <- list(row = bootstrap_row, stratified = bootstrap_stratified,
                   cluster = bootstrap_cluster, two_way = bootstrap_two_way) |>
    map(\(bootstrap) bootstrap(df_cells, K))

  # Average pathologist: metrics over all resampled cells of a draw
  df_average <- df_draws[c("row", "cluster", "two_way")] |>
    map(\(df) df |> group_by(.draw) |> calc_metrics()) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "method") |>
    mutate(estimand = "average_pathologist")

  # Single pathologist: metrics per draw and pathologist, the draws of all pathologists combined
  # (not for the row bootstrap; two_way gives the same distribution as cluster)
  df_single <- df_draws[c("stratified", "cluster")] |>
    map(\(df) df |> group_by(.draw, rater_ID) |> calc_metrics()) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "method") |>
    mutate(estimand = "single_pathologist")

  # Point estimate: the metrics of the original dataset (average pathologist)
  df_observed <- df_cells |>
    calc_metrics() |>
    mutate(estimand = "average_pathologist") |>
    rename(value_observed = value)

  bind_rows(df_average, df_single) |>
    group_by(method, estimand, name, averaging) |>
    median_interval() |>
    left_join(df_observed, by = c("estimand", "name", "averaging"))
}
```

# Settings
```{r}
n_workers     <- 11
K             <- 10000
dir_estimates <- "simulation/estimates_pathologists"
```

# Load data
```{r}
df_seed_offsets <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_seed_offsets.csv")
df_counts       <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_1_pathologist_observed_data.csv.xz")

offset_bootstrap <- df_seed_offsets |> filter(step == "bootstrap") |> pull(offset)
```

# Jobs
```{r}
df_jobs <- df_counts |>
  nest(data = c(slide, rater_ID, P, TP, FN, FP)) |>
  mutate(seed_bootstrap = seed + offset_bootstrap) |>
  arrange(rep, scenario, n_slide, variant)

nrow(df_jobs)
```

# Bootstrap
```{r}
dir.create(dir_estimates, showWarnings = FALSE)

mirai::daemons(n_workers)
invisible(mirai::everywhere(
  {
    library(dplyr)
    library(tidyr)
    library(purrr)
    library(tidybayes)
  },
  K = K, median_interval = median_interval, calc_metrics = calc_metrics,
  bootstrap_row = bootstrap_row, bootstrap_stratified = bootstrap_stratified,
  bootstrap_cluster = bootstrap_cluster, bootstrap_two_way = bootstrap_two_way,
  bootstrap_pathologist_metrics = bootstrap_pathologist_metrics
))

t_start <- Sys.time()
df_bootstrap_estimates <- df_jobs |>
  split(seq_len(nrow(df_jobs))) |>
  map(in_parallel(\(job) {
    set.seed(job$seed_bootstrap)
    bootstrap_pathologist_metrics(job$data[[1]], K) |>
      mutate(scenario = job$scenario, n_slide = job$n_slide, rep = job$rep, variant = job$variant)
  }), .progress = TRUE) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(model = paste0("Bootstrap, ", method), model_id = paste0("bootstrap_", method)) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, model, model_id, estimand, averaging, name, interval,
         value, value_observed, .lower, .upper)
mirai::daemons(0)

difftime(Sys.time(), t_start, units = "mins")

write_csv(df_bootstrap_estimates, file.path(dir_estimates, "06_1_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz"))
```

# Check
```{r}
# Number of datasets per method, estimand and variant
df_bootstrap_estimates |>
  distinct(model_id, estimand, scenario, rep, variant) |>
  count(model_id, estimand, variant, name = "datasets")

# Interval width per method (F1, QI): the row bootstrap should be the narrowest
df_bootstrap_estimates |>
  filter(name == "F1", interval == "qi") |>
  group_by(estimand, averaging, variant, model_id) |>
  summarise(mean_width = mean(.upper - .lower), .groups = "drop")
```
